standards.title: ZLIB Compressed Data Format Specification version 3.3

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic case-insensitive normative must, should, and recommended clauses in specifications without a BCP 14 keyword convention; may, optional, and need-not permissions are excluded.

requirements.summary: The bounded zlib decoder accepts and decompresses conforming byte-aligned zlib streams within the caller's explicit resource contract.
The Deflate content encoder produces a complete conforming zlib wrapper rather than a raw DEFLATE stream.
Encoded CMF and FLG bytes satisfy the RFC modulo-31 FCHECK invariant.
The compressor emits the required CMF and FLG header and the correct terminal ADLER32 checksum.
HTTP Deflate encoding rejects caller dictionary state and therefore never sets FDICT for this embedding format.
The decoder validates CMF, FLG, and ADLER32 independently and reports malformed input on any incorrect value.
A syntactically checkable header using an unsupported compression method is rejected as invalid encoding.
An FDICT stream whose DICTID has no authorized preset dictionary is rejected with a typed dictionary error.
A zlib embedding format must support every preset dictionary that the embedding format specifies.
requirements.reason: The HTTP Deflate content coding implemented here specifies no zlib preset dictionaries; dictionary transport uses separately typed Brotli and Zstandard codings and never reaches the zlib wrapper.

requirements.summary: Because HTTP Deflate defines no preset dictionary, every received zlib stream carrying FDICT is rejected.
A compressor and decompressor using the optional zlib dictionary feature must use exactly the same dictionary.
requirements.reason: The public HTTP Deflate coding rejects dictionaries on both encode and decode, so no zlib preset-dictionary session can be established or mismatched.

requirements.summary: A standard data format using zlib preset dictionaries must define its allowed dictionaries precisely.
requirements.reason: This package implements existing HTTP content codings and does not define a standard data format that embeds zlib with the optional preset-dictionary feature.

requirements.summary: The ADLER32 calculation begins with the required recommended initial checksum value of one.

standards.title: DEFLATE Compressed Data Format Specification version 1.3

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic case-insensitive normative must, should, and recommended clauses in specifications without a BCP 14 keyword convention; may, optional, and need-not permissions are excluded.

requirements.summary: The bounded DEFLATE decoder accepts conforming stored, fixed-Huffman, dynamic-Huffman, and maximum-range streams.
The Deflate content encoder emits complete conforming DEFLATE data inside the required zlib wrapper.
DEFLATE block fields and Huffman codes use the RFC's defined bit-to-byte packing order without host-endian dependence.
The compressor does not emit Huffman codes beyond the format maxima and the decoder rejects malformed dynamic trees.
Symbols with zero bit length receive no Huffman value in emitted trees and malformed tree assignments are rejected.
Length and distance extra-bit integers are interpreted least-significant bit first as corrected by reported erratum 7764.
Zero-length literal, length, and distance symbols do not participate in Huffman tree construction.
The decoder accepts the maximum 258-byte match and 32768-byte backward distance defined by DEFLATE.
The streaming decoder accepts large and multi-block representations subject only to the caller's explicit finite resource limits.
A compressor implementor is strongly recommended to follow the historical algorithm described to avoid then-relevant patent coverage.
requirements.reason: The repository does not implement or redistribute a DEFLATE compression algorithm; it uses the explicitly permitted OTP runtime zlib service, and this historical patent rationale is not wire behavior.

requirements.summary: Systems using DEFLATE provide an integrity check for compressed data instead of silently accepting corruption.

entries.reason: The published MSB-first sentence conflicts with the section 3.1 packing rule and interoperable DEFLATE wire behavior; the proposed LSB-first correction is applied.
The proposed insertion of the word length disambiguates the prose but does not alter the defined Huffman construction or interoperable decoder behavior.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic case-insensitive normative must, should, and recommended clauses in specifications without a BCP 14 keyword convention; may, optional, and need-not permissions are excluded.

requirements.summary: The bounded gzip decoder accepts conforming minimal, optional-header, and concatenated-member representations.
The gzip encoder emits a deterministic complete member with a conforming header, DEFLATE payload, and trailer.
An emitted optional original filename must consist only of ISO 8859-1 characters.
requirements.reason: The public HTTP gzip encoder accepts content bytes only and always emits the minimal deterministic header with FNAME clear, so it cannot emit filename metadata in any character set.

requirements.summary: A filename from an operating system using another character set must be translated into ISO 8859-1.
requirements.reason: No filesystem filename or filename encoding enters the content-coding API and the encoder always leaves FNAME clear; operating-system name translation is therefore unreachable.

requirements.summary: An emitted optional gzip comment must consist only of ISO 8859-1 characters.
requirements.reason: The encoder exposes no comment metadata and emits the deterministic minimal gzip header with FCOMMENT clear, so it cannot serialize a nonconforming comment.

requirements.summary: Line breaks in an emitted optional gzip comment should use one line-feed byte.
requirements.reason: The public encoder never emits FCOMMENT and accepts no comment text, leaving no line-ending metadata to normalize.

requirements.summary: The three reserved bits in every emitted gzip FLG byte are zero.
The compressor emits correct ID1, ID2, compression method, CRC32, and uncompressed input size fields.
The compliant gzip compressor sets every reserved header flag bit to zero.
The decoder validates both gzip identification bytes and compression method and rejects every incorrect value.
The decoder parses or skips bounded FEXTRA, XLEN, FNAME, FCOMMENT, and FHCRC fields before the compressed payload.
A gzip member with any nonzero reserved FLG bit is rejected rather than misparsed as a known header layout.
The gzip decoder validates the CRC32 integrity field and fails closed on compressed-data corruption.

entries.reason: The verified correction updates obsolete scheme-design guidance from RFC 2718 to RFC 4395 and changes no URI grammar or runtime behavior.
The verified correction removes an accidental hyperlink from an algorithm example and has no source-text or resolution behavior effect.
The unverified proposal would add backslash to unreserved characters despite the published ABNF and established URI processing; the strict redirect boundary retains the published grammar.
The held proposal adds host-language slash delimiters and escapes to an illustrative regular expression; the product does not use that non-validating appendix expression.
The held clarification of abnormal excess-parent examples is not a verified grammar change; executable resolution vectors retain the published remove-dot-segments behavior.
The held alternative merge rule for a base ending in slash-dot-dot has not updated STD 66, so the standards-library merge algorithm remains authoritative.
The held host-prose proposal does not alter the published reg-name ABNF; HTTP redirect admission separately requires a nonempty validated authority.
The held proposal adds a redundant path-abempty alternative to relative-part; slash references already resolve through the published path-absolute alternative.
Replacing the zero-repetition spelling of path-empty with an empty quoted string only clarifies equivalent ABNF and changes no accepted URI.
The held pseudocode wording would pass the base object rather than naming only its path; the following merge procedure already uses the base authority and behavior is unchanged.
The rejected proposal would add hash to fragment content and therefore does not modify the published URI-reference grammar.
The rejected proposal incorrectly makes scheme mandatory in a URI-reference, whose relative-ref production deliberately permits no scheme.
The rejected dec-octet alternative reordering addresses parser strategy rather than ABNF validity and does not change IPv4 syntax.
The rejected expanded IPv6 grammar is not a correction to the equivalent published alternatives and cannot change accepted address literals.
The rejected proposal inserts a hash into the scheme capture of the illustrative regular expression contrary to the deliberate URI-reference syntax.
The rejected report supplied no actionable corrected text for the explicitly non-validating appendix parser and changes no normative grammar.
The rejected URL-only wording was superseded by verified erratum 2525's updated URI-scheme reference and has no runtime effect.
The rejected proposal confuses the four hier-part path forms with the five general path forms and does not alter the published ABNF.

standards.title: The Base16, Base32, and Base64 Data Encodings

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: Base64 serialization never inserts line feeds or other folding characters into encoded output.
Structured Field Byte Sequence serialization includes the exact required terminal Base64 padding.
Base64 input containing whitespace, URL-safe substitutions, or any character outside the selected alphabet is rejected.
Encoders emit zero unused pad bits and decoders reject noncanonical encodings whose discarded pad bits are nonzero.

entries.reason: The verified correction fixes an off-by-one archival reference URL and does not change any Base-N alphabet or encoding behavior.
The verified note clarifies that displayed test strings denote input octets; executable vectors use explicit byte arrays and are unaffected.
The verified subject-verb correction changes prose only and leaves the zero-pad-bit requirement unchanged.
The verified change replaces the indefinite article before URI and has no URL-safe alphabet or padding effect.
The unverified proposal clarifies Base32 final input grouping; this product publishes only the standard Base64 form required by Structured Fields.
The reported addition states the bit order already implied by the published octet and six-bit-group algorithm, so interoperable Base64 wire bytes do not change.

requirements.summary: Include every handshake message associated with RFC 6066 extensions in the transcript hash used by Finished.
requirements.reason: The custom TLS engine appends complete encoded handshake messages before computing and checking Finished. The SNI acknowledgement test proves that removing an extension-bearing EncryptedExtensions invalidates the authenticated transcript at CertificateVerify, and a general tampered-Finished test exists. No test mutates an extension-bearing message while holding Finished fixed in both directions, and the OTP paths remain provider boundaries, so the exact Finished obligation lacks complete executable proof.

bounded_verification_task.acceptance_focus: Authenticate every sent RFC 6066 extension-bearing message in both endpoint directions and supported TLS providers.
bounded_verification_task.maximum_scope: Focused transcript mutation probes for the custom TLS 1.3 engine and version-pinned OTP 28/29 peers; no public API change.
acceptance: Mutate one byte in each sent RFC 6066 extension-bearing handshake message while leaving the Finished value unchanged and require a Finished failure in both endpoint directions.
Record only extension kind, direction, fixed outcome, provider identity, and source digest; retain no handshake traffic secrets.
Break transcript inclusion deliberately and prove the focused test fails.

requirements.summary: When attempting session resumption, send the same RFC 6066 extensions that a fresh ClientHello would send.
requirements.reason: The custom TLS client builds SNI and other base extensions before appending the PSK extensions, but existing tests do not compare the complete fresh and resumed RFC 6066 extension sets. The OTP client does not configure a session-ticket mode, and current tests do not establish whether resumption is reachable or what it sends.

bounded_verification_task.acceptance_focus: Compare fresh and resumed RFC 6066 ClientHello extensions on custom TLS and OTP 28/29.
bounded_verification_task.maximum_scope: Focused fresh/resumed ClientHello and server response probes for custom TLS plus OTP 28/29; no session-cache redesign.
acceptance: Prove a resumed client repeats the original SNI and other RFC 6066 extensions that a fresh connection would send.
Prove a different SNI cannot resume the original session and instead takes a full-handshake path.
Prove a resumed response omits the SNI acknowledgement while a full handshake that uses SNI acknowledges it, with exact TLS 1.2/TLS 1.3 placement.
Determine OTP client and server resumption reachability from wire evidence rather than provider defaults.

requirements.summary: If a pre-TLS-1.3 older session is resumed, ignore the offered RFC 6066 extensions, send none of these extension types in ServerHello, and retain the original session extension functionality.
requirements.reason: The only pre-TLS-1.3 server path explicitly sets reuse_sessions to false, which makes the older-session condition unreachable. The custom QUIC engine is TLS 1.3 only, where RFC 8446 defines different PSK and extension-placement rules.

requirements.summary: Encode server_name extension_data as the RFC 6066 ServerNameList structure.
requirements.reason: The custom encoder has an exact canonical vector and the OTP client explicitly passes one server_name_indication value. The current suite does not independently observe the OTP ClientHello bytes, so the provider-backed HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 path remains an evidence gap rather than an inferred conformance claim.

bounded_verification_task.acceptance_focus: Capture and validate the exact OTP and custom-TLS ServerNameList encoding without retaining the hostname.
bounded_verification_task.maximum_scope: One independent bounded TLS peer plus SNI decoder fuzz corpus on OTP 28/29 and custom TLS; no certificate-policy expansion.
acceptance: Capture the exact OTP ClientHello ServerNameList shape without recording the hostname value and compare it with the canonical custom-TLS vector.
Exercise empty, duplicate-type, truncated, oversized, and inconsistent nested lengths against every server path under an absolute deadline.
Assert typed failure, bounded memory, no crash, and no retained worker or socket; deliberately remove a length guard and prove detection.

requirements.summary: Do not emit or accept more than one server name of the same NameType in one ServerNameList.
requirements.reason: The public inputs provide one DNS name and the custom encoder emits one host_name entry. The custom decoder and complete ClientHello path now reject a second host_name with typed DuplicateIdentifier(0), with focused regression and mutation evidence. The OTP-backed server path still lacks a crafted duplicate-NameType rejection and cleanup probe, so the project-wide claim remains Open rather than inferring provider behavior.

bounded_verification_task.acceptance_focus: Construct duplicate host_name entries for custom and OTP server paths and prove rejection under a bounded deadline.
bounded_verification_task.maximum_scope: One independent bounded TLS peer plus SNI decoder fuzz corpus on OTP 28/29 and custom TLS; no certificate-policy expansion.
acceptance: Capture the exact OTP ClientHello ServerNameList shape without recording the hostname value and compare it with the canonical custom-TLS vector.
Exercise empty, duplicate-type, truncated, oversized, and inconsistent nested lengths against every server path under an absolute deadline.

requirements.summary: For an understood but unrecognized SNI, either abort with fatal unrecognized_name or continue.
requirements.reason: RFC 9325 Section 3.7 updates this permissive RFC 6066 choice: a server should not continue and should send fatal unrecognized_name. Closure must therefore be judged against the later stricter obligation, not by selecting RFC 6066 continuation.

requirements.summary: Do not send a warning-level unrecognized_name alert for an unrecognized SNI.
requirements.reason: No library code intentionally constructs a warning-level alert, but the HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 server delegates alert behavior to OTP and the custom server currently falls back to its default credential for an unknown name. No focused test observes the alert level, so provider behavior is not presumed.

bounded_verification_task.acceptance_focus: Prove warning-level unrecognized_name is never emitted and retain the RFC 9325 fatal behavior as the governing target.
bounded_verification_task.maximum_scope: Focused unknown-SNI peer tests for each server TLS path and version; no new credential API.
acceptance: Observe the alert level and outcome for a well-formed but unrecognized DNS SNI on TLS 1.2 and 1.3.
Reject warning-level unrecognized_name and preserve the stricter RFC 9325 fatal-alert requirement as a separate implementation gate.
Assert no request bytes reach an application after a fatal SNI decision.

requirements.summary: Define every future NameType data structure with an initial 16-bit length field.
requirements.reason: The library implements only RFC 6066 host_name and does not define or register a new NameType. This is a protocol-extension designer constraint, not a runtime obligation triggered by the public API.

requirements.summary: Include server_name in ClientHello when a client locates a server by a supported DNS name.
requirements.reason: The OTP client always supplies the authentication name as server_name_indication. The custom QUIC client encodes config.hostname for DNS names and omits SNI for IP literals. Existing authenticated-handshake, exact-vector, live SNI credential-selection, and IP-literal tests cover both branches of the custom path.

requirements.summary: When a server uses offered SNI for credential or security-policy selection, acknowledge server_name in its response flight.
requirements.reason: The custom TLS 1.3 server now records whether exact or wildcard SNI selected an alternative credential and emits exactly one empty server_name acknowledgement in EncryptedExtensions only for that full handshake. Focused tests cover exact and wildcard selection, unused and absent SNI, HelloRetryRequest, authenticated transcript inclusion, and omission on resumption. The OTP-backed HTTP server has no SNI credential selector, so this requirement's antecedent remains inactive there.

requirements.summary: Encode the server_name acknowledgement with empty extension_data.
requirements.reason: The server encodes the server_name acknowledgement with zero extension bytes. The client accepts that form only after offering DNS SNI on a full handshake and rejects non-empty, unsolicited, and resumed acknowledgements with typed InvalidConfiguration failures. Focused tests authenticate the acknowledgement in the transcript and kill mutations that disable the full-handshake acknowledgement or admit it on resumption or without an SNI offer.

requirements.summary: Send the same server_name extension on a resumption attempt as on the full handshake that established the session.
requirements.reason: Custom session tickets bind a server name and client_extensions retains the ordinary SNI extension when a ticket is offered. Existing tests complete resumption, but do not compare the exact SNI bytes between full and resumed ClientHello. OTP 28/29 reachability and wire behavior are untested.

bounded_verification_task.acceptance_focus: Assert byte-for-byte SNI continuity from the establishing handshake to every resumption attempt.
bounded_verification_task.maximum_scope: Focused fresh/resumed ClientHello and server response probes for custom TLS plus OTP 28/29; no session-cache redesign.

Prove a resumed response omits the SNI acknowledgement while a full handshake that uses SNI acknowledges it, with exact TLS 1.2/TLS 1.3 placement.

requirements.summary: Do not resume a session under a different SNI; perform a full handshake instead.
requirements.reason: The custom ticket opening path binds the expected name, and a focused test shows a different expected name produces FullHandshake. The OTP TLS 1.2 server disables reuse, but TLS 1.3 ticket reachability is not explicitly pinned or tested, so the full server surface cannot yet be closed.

requirements.summary: Do not include a server_name acknowledgement when resuming a session.
requirements.reason: The custom server now emits the empty SNI acknowledgement only when a full handshake used SNI and explicitly omits it for a selected resumed session; the client also rejects a forged acknowledgement on that resumed path. OTP TLS 1.3 ticket reachability and response bytes remain unpinned, so the project-wide row stays Open until the provider boundary is measured.

bounded_verification_task.acceptance_focus: After full-handshake acknowledgement exists, prove every resumed response omits SNI acknowledgement.

requirements.summary: When an application negotiates a server name before upgrading to TLS, use that same name in SNI.
requirements.reason: HTTP transports in this repository do not negotiate a server name in an application protocol and then upgrade that connection to TLS. Cleartext and TLS use separate connect/listen modes, so the conditional protocol shape is absent.

requirements.summary: After TLS establishes server_name, do not request a different server name at the application layer.
requirements.reason: HTTP requests carry an authority and HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 can intentionally coalesce certificate-authorized origins; the library exposes no application-layer server-name renegotiation mechanism corresponding to this RFC 6066 condition.

requirements.summary: Encode a requested maximum_fragment_length as one allowed MaxFragmentLength enum value.
requirements.reason: RFC 6066 makes this extension opt-in. The public client API exposes no constrained TLS-record size and neither option builder nor the custom TLS extension set requests it, so no library-owned negotiation state triggers the encoding rule.

requirements.summary: If accepting maximum_fragment_length, echo the same requested enum value.
requirements.reason: No server API opts into this optional feature and the custom TLS engine has no such extension. Because the library does not advertise maximum-fragment negotiation, the conditional acknowledgement rule is outside the declared surface.

requirements.summary: Abort with illegal_parameter when the requested maximum fragment value is invalid.
requirements.reason: The optional extension is not exposed or intentionally negotiated by either server path. Malformed TLS handshake size remains governed by separate bounded parser limits, not an advertised maximum_fragment_length capability.

requirements.summary: Abort with illegal_parameter when the server response differs from the requested maximum fragment value.
requirements.reason: The client never offers the optional extension through the library API, so it cannot receive a valid in-context acknowledgement that triggers this comparison.

requirements.summary: Begin fragmenting records to the negotiated smaller maximum immediately after negotiation.
requirements.reason: No public configuration offers or accepts this optional record-size profile; therefore there is no negotiated smaller maximum in library-owned state.

requirements.summary: Discard an oversized record and send record_overflow before decrypting it when maximum_fragment_length is active.
requirements.reason: The extension cannot be enabled through the library and is absent from the custom TLS engine. Ordinary TLS record parsing and QUIC packet limits do not make this conditional RFC 6066 feature applicable.

requirements.summary: For DTLS with maximum_fragment_length, do not send record_overflow unless the packet first passes message authentication.
requirements.reason: The library has no DTLS endpoint, and its UDP transport is QUIC. Both the protocol and extension antecedents are false.

requirements.summary: Encode client_certificate_url ClientHello extension_data as empty.
requirements.reason: The public client credential APIs send certificates in-band and never offer client_certificate_url. The optional URL-fetch feature is absent by design, so its encoding branch is unreachable.

requirements.summary: A server accepting client_certificate_url must acknowledge it with empty extension_data.
requirements.reason: Neither server path accepts or exposes client certificate URLs. The OTP HTTP server currently disables client authentication, and custom HTTP/3 mTLS accepts only in-band certificate messages.

requirements.summary: Require every CertificateURL URL to be an absolute immediately usable URI reference.
requirements.reason: No API constructs, accepts, fetches, or exposes CertificateURL, so no URL enters a library-owned certificate authentication path.

requirements.summary: Encode the URLAndHash padding byte as 0x01.
requirements.reason: The unsupported optional extension has no URLAndHash encoder or decoder in the product surface.

requirements.summary: Retrieve a received client certificate chain from its URLs and then process the chain normally.
requirements.reason: The server never negotiates client_certificate_url and has no network fetcher in TLS authentication. Adding implicit certificate URL retrieval would also introduce an unbounded SSRF-capable surface that is not a declared feature.

requirements.summary: A server implementing certificate URL retrieval must support the http URI scheme.
requirements.reason: The library implements no TLS certificate-URL retrieval role, so this positive scheme requirement is not triggered by an advertised capability.

requirements.summary: Do not follow HTTP redirects while retrieving a certificate URL.
requirements.reason: There is no certificate URL fetch operation. Ordinary HTTP redirect support is not invoked from TLS authentication and cannot trigger this extension-specific constraint.

requirements.summary: Do not choose certificate URLs whose retrieval depends on HTTP redirects.
requirements.reason: No client API emits a CertificateURL or accepts a certificate URI, so there is no application-controlled URL list to validate.

requirements.summary: Use application/pkix-cert or application/pkix-pkipath for MIME-formatted certificate URL responses.
requirements.reason: The library is neither a CertificateURL publisher nor a TLS certificate URL retriever. Its ordinary HTTP MIME behavior does not claim this optional TLS role.

requirements.summary: Verify that each fetched certificate object matches the SHA-1 hash carried in URLAndHash.
requirements.reason: No server path negotiates or fetches CertificateURL objects, so no RFC 6066 SHA-1 URLAndHash verification state exists.

requirements.summary: Abort with fatal bad_certificate_hash_value when a fetched object hash mismatches.
requirements.reason: The unsupported feature cannot produce a fetched object or URLAndHash comparison. No alert emitter for this optional path is exposed.

requirements.summary: Send fatal certificate_unobtainable when a required client certificate cannot be retrieved.
requirements.reason: The library never accepts URL-delivered client certificates, so it cannot make certificate authentication depend on retrieving one.

requirements.summary: On a warning-level certificate_unobtainable alert, log it and continue if possible.
requirements.reason: No client offers client_certificate_url, and diagnostics intentionally do not expose raw TLS alert payloads. The optional warning condition is unreachable.

requirements.summary: Encode trusted_ca_keys extension_data as TrustedAuthorities.
requirements.reason: Trust configuration supplies complete anchors for certificate validation; it does not advertise a constrained root-key subset through RFC 6066 trusted_ca_keys. No public option enables this optional hint.

requirements.summary: When using trusted_ca_keys to select a chain, acknowledge the extension in the server response.
requirements.reason: Neither server credential selector consumes this extension, so it cannot influence certificate-chain selection and the conditional acknowledgement is not triggered.

requirements.summary: Encode the trusted_ca_keys server acknowledgement with empty extension_data.
requirements.reason: The optional extension is never accepted or acknowledged by the library API.

requirements.summary: If truncated_hmac is ever offered, encode its ClientHello extension_data as empty.
requirements.reason: The public API does not expose truncated_hmac, but the OTP paths have no explicit exclusion or negative negotiation test. RFC 8446 Appendix D and RFC 9325 Section 4.6 later require implementations not to use it, so leaving provider defaults unowned cannot justify NotApplicable.

bounded_implementation_task.acceptance_focus: Make the extension unofferable and verify a peer cannot cause its negotiation.
bounded_implementation_task.maximum_scope: Explicit TLS extension policy at both OTP option builders plus one custom-TLS registry invariant and focused negative peers.
acceptance: Make truncated_hmac offering and acceptance unreachable for every TLS 1.2 endpoint path, consistent with RFC 8446 and RFC 9325.
Fail the gate when an OTP upgrade can negotiate a 10-byte truncated HMAC under the exact supported runtime versions.
Keep diagnostics to fixed outcome codes and deliberately relax the exclusion to prove test sensitivity.

requirements.summary: If truncated_hmac is negotiated with an HMAC suite, use and verify exactly the first 10 HMAC bytes.
requirements.reason: The desired secure design forbids reaching this legacy 80-bit-MAC state, but no explicit library-owned policy or focused peer test currently proves it unreachable on OTP TLS 1.2. Implementing the modern prohibition closes this conditional row without implementing truncated MAC records.

requirements.reason: OTP supports a client stapling option but client_tls_options does not expose or set it; the custom TLS extension enum only recognizes status_request as opaque and client_extensions never sends it. The shipped user-agent boundary is an opt-in, finite, network-partitioned service-client cookie store with deterministic clocks, typed persistence deadlines, canonical hosts, exact path and attribute processing, single-field serialization, bounded eviction, and lifecycle cleanup. Origin-server authoring and application security guidance, intermediary behavior, browser UI, private-browsing policy, and non-HTTP APIs are explicit role boundaries.

requirements.summary: Expired entries are removed before every store operation and an already-expired replacement removes its prior key.
Capacity enforcement first prunes expired entries and then retains the most recently used entries within global count and byte limits.
Matching request cookies are promoted as one bounded access operation so later capacity eviction removes the least recently accessed peer.
Session cookies remain live only for one Client, remove any persisted prior key, and all in-memory state is destroyed on close.

The proposed text makes status 1011 endpoint-neutral. The shared close validator accepts 1011 for both client and server roles.
The correction renames a masked Ping response in an example to Pong. The bytes and opcode in the published example are already unchanged.
The proposed mixed-content step belongs to a browser settings object and entry script. This non-browser networking library has neither concept.
The corrected lowercase websocket Upgrade token matches emitted request and response fields; validation remains ASCII case-insensitive as RFC 6455 requires.
The RFC Editor rejected the objection to unpredictable masking, so the strong fresh-mask requirements and implementation remain unchanged.
The RFC Editor confirmed that the field is 64 bits wide while its value space is restricted to 63 bits; the existing decoder keeps the high-bit check.
The report proposed additional fragmentation guidance rather than correcting the RFC. Existing finite per-frame and reassembled-message limits remain independently enforced.

standards.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)

requirements.summary: A valid Strict-Transport-Security response establishes policy for the emitting host and later HTTP loads enforce that policy.

Ignore syntactically valid directives whose names are not recognized.

A usable STS field contains exactly one max-age directive.

requirements.reason: The server package is a protocol-neutral handler runtime and exposes no HSTS-host declaration or automatic STS emission policy. An application that chooses to emit this response field owns whether to declare itself an HSTS Host.

requirements.summary: An STS field emitted by an HSTS Host must satisfy the Section 6.1 grammar.
requirements.reason: The server deliberately treats application response fields as opaque bytes and provides no HSTS field constructor or HSTS-host mode. The application that supplies an STS value owns its grammar.

requirements.summary: An HSTS Host that emits STS must include only one such response field.

requirements.summary: An HSTS Host must not emit STS in a response conveyed over insecure transport.
requirements.reason: The server never emits STS automatically and does not claim to validate arbitrary application response fields as an HSTS deployment policy. Applications that add this opaque field own the secure-transport precondition.

requirements.summary: A valid STS field received after an error-free authenticated HTTPS exchange notes a new policy or refreshes the exact host policy from the current reception time.
A max-age value of zero removes the exact host policy, including its includeSubDomains assertion, from live and configured persistent storage.
A max-age value of zero never retains a policy for a previously unknown host.
When a response contains multiple STS fields, process only the first field even when it is invalid.
Never learn, refresh, or delete HSTS policy from a response received over insecure HTTP.
A malformed first STS field is ignored and cannot be replaced by a later STS field in the same response.
IPv4 addresses, non-canonical IPv4 spellings, and IPv6 literals are never stored as Known HSTS Hosts.
Store a new exact host with its advertised expiry and includeSubDomains state in the finite, network-partitioned policy store.
Learning or refreshing an exact subdomain policy uses that exact canonical host key and never changes a matched superdomain policy.
The policy owner removes expired entries on receipt and at a finite timer deadline; matching also excludes entries at their exact expiry boundary.
Before each initial or redirected HTTP exchange, canonicalize and match its host against the current HSTS store.
Match exact hosts and asserted includeSubDomains policies case-insensitively on DNS label boundaries, excluding expired entries and IP addresses.
A matching HTTP request is converted to HTTPS before transport selection or transmission.
A matching HTTP URI with explicit port 80 is upgraded to explicit port 443.
A matching HTTP URI with an explicit port other than 80 preserves that port while changing the scheme.
A matching HTTP URI without an explicit port remains without an explicit port after its scheme is upgraded.

HSTS upgrades retain mandatory certificate-chain and service-identity authentication for TCP TLS and QUIC TLS; any authentication or transport error terminates the attempt without an insecure fallback.
A user agent must not derive HSTS policy from an HTML http-equiv meta element.
requirements.reason: Response bodies are opaque bounded byte streams and this library has no HTML parser, DOM, or meta-element processing path, so content can never reach the HSTS header learner.

requirements.summary: A secure response without an STS field leaves the existing policy unchanged, and the host remains upgraded until its monotonic expiry.
An HSTS Host comparing effective request URIs must distinguish an empty path component from an absolute slash path.
requirements.reason: The package exposes parsed request targets to a handler but has no HSTS-host effective-request-URI comparison operation. Applications performing such HSTS site comparisons own this semantic step.

requirements.summary: Canonicalize and validate internationalized host labels with nontransitional UTS 46 processing built from IDNA2008 properties before HSTS storage or matching.
A user agent lacking IDNA2008 must implement IDNA2003.
requirements.reason: The activating condition is false: the host pipeline implements nontransitional UTS 46 with IDNA2008-derived validity, bidi, joining, normalization, and Punycode processing.

standards.review_scope: All 34 atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses are dispositioned. The shipped HSTS contract is a bounded, network-partitioned origin-client policy: it learns only from completed authenticated HTTPS responses, matches canonical DNS hosts, upgrades requests before transport, and never parses response bodies. Generic server response fields remain application-owned because the server exposes no HSTS-host declaration or emission mode; those deployment duties and server-side effective-URI comparison are explicitly NotApplicable.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

entries.reason: The proposed includeParent cookie-injection discussion was rejected as a possible future protocol update rather than an error in RFC 6797. The published downward-only includeSubDomains policy is retained.

The proposed spelling change was rejected: directive names are already case-insensitive, while include-sub-domains would be a different registered name. The parser retains the published includeSubDomains name with case-insensitive matching.
The report was rejected because receiving the same max-age later conveys a different absolute expiry. Each valid reception therefore refreshes the policy from its current monotonic reception time.

The proposed localhost exception would add new normative behavior and was rejected as outside the errata process. The published rule has no localhost exception, and authenticated localhost can be noted.
The proposed ABNF slash was rejected because RFC 6797 explicitly uses the RFC 2616 BNF convention, where vertical bar denotes alternatives. Token and quoted-string directive values remain accepted.

requirements.summary: Changing the HTTP/3 destination port never changes the URI, origin authority, TLS identity, or request authority visible to the application.

requirements.summary: Percent-encode a percent octet when serializing an ALPN protocol name in an Alt-Svc field.
requirements.reason: No server or proxy Alt-Svc serializer is part of the public library surface, and the sole consumed protocol identifier is the literal h3 token, which contains no percent octet.

requirements.summary: Do not percent-encode valid token octets other than percent when serializing an Alt-Svc protocol identifier.
requirements.reason: The library never serializes Alt-Svc protocol identifiers; its same-host HTTP/3 discovery accepts only the unescaped literal h3 token and ignores every unsupported identifier.

requirements.summary: Use uppercase hexadecimal digits whenever an ALPN protocol identifier requires percent encoding.
requirements.reason: No Alt-Svc field generator or general ALPN protocol-id codec exists in this library, and the supported literal h3 identifier does not enter a percent-encoding path.

requirements.summary: An HTTP/2 origin server advertising alternative services should prefer the ALTSVC frame over repeated response fields.
requirements.reason: The HTTP/2 server API does not advertise alternative services and deliberately has no ALTSVC frame producer; the completed scope is the integrated client's authenticated same-host HTTP/3 discovery.

requirements.summary: Unknown Alt-Svc parameters do not reject or otherwise alter a supported h3 alternative.
A supported alt-value is processed with the same port and freshness semantics when an unknown parameter is present.
The supported port-only alt-authority processes RFC 7230 quoted-pair escaping before validating the bounded port.
A persist parameter whose value is not 1 is ignored without discarding the otherwise valid alternative.
Ignore an ALTSVC frame whose Origin is not authoritative for the current HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.reason: The integrated client does not implement or consume the RFC 7838 HTTP/2 ALTSVC extension frame, so no frame Origin can cross the HTTP/2 boundary or affect its Alt-Svc store.

requirements.summary: A device acting as an HTTP/2 server ignores an incoming ALTSVC frame.
requirements.reason: RFC 7838 ALTSVC frame support is outside the HTTP/2 server surface; the server neither registers this extension frame as an application event nor uses it to update alternative-service state.

requirements.summary: Ignore an ALTSVC frame on stream zero whose Origin field is empty.
requirements.reason: The client has no RFC 7838 ALTSVC frame decoder or frame-to-store path; its discovery inputs are authenticated HTTPS response fields and authenticated HTTPS records only.

requirements.summary: Ignore an ALTSVC frame on a nonzero stream when it contains a non-empty Origin field.
requirements.reason: No ALTSVC frame parser or origin-association API exists in the integrated HTTP/2 client, so this invalid frame form cannot create or replace a retained route.

requirements.summary: An HTTP intermediary does not forward hop-by-hop ALTSVC frames.
requirements.reason: This project exposes request proxying and MASQUE facilities but no general HTTP/2 intermediary that receives and forwards extension frames, and it does not implement the ALTSVC frame type.

requirements.summary: Every request sent through a selected HTTP/3 alternative carries Alt-Used with the actual alternative authority.
A 421 response received through HTTP/3 immediately expires the corresponding origin's alternative-service entry.
An Alt-Svc field carried by a 421 response cannot replace the entry that the response invalidates.
A request to register a new Alt-Svc parameter includes its parameter name and a pointer to specification text.
requirements.reason: The library neither defines a new Alt-Svc extension parameter nor submits entries to the IANA registry; registration procedure and change control remain outside its runtime and distribution interfaces.

requirements.summary: Internationalized domain names in an Alt-Svc field or ALTSVC frame are expressed as DNS A-labels.
requirements.reason: The client accepts only a port-only same-host alt-authority and emits no Alt-Svc field, while the HTTP/2 ALTSVC frame is unsupported; therefore no internationalized host is serialized or consumed in either RFC 7838 wire location.

requirements.summary: Any configured certificate-pin validation applies equally to direct and alternative connections for the origin.
requirements.reason: The public client has no certificate-pin policy or pin callback to apply on either route; mandatory trust-chain and origin-identity verification is always applied, but the conditional certificate-pinning feature named by this clause is absent.

requirements.summary: A user agent removes alternative-service information when it clears origin-specific data such as cookies.
requirements.reason: This library is not a browser user agent and exposes no origin-data clearing operation that combines cookies, cache, HSTS, and Alt-Svc state; closing the owned Client releases its finite in-memory stores, while application persistence adapters remain caller-owned.

standards.title: Happy Eyeballs Version 2: Better Connectivity Using Concurrency

requirements.summary: Start AAAA resolution first and start A resolution immediately afterward when both destination families are enabled.
Do not wait for both address families to finish resolving before beginning a usable connection attempt.
Resolve IPv4 and IPv6 independently in supervised work so a stalled resolver cannot block the other family.
When an A result arrives before AAAA, wait the bounded Resolution Delay before starting the IPv4 candidate.
Proceed with available IPv4 destinations when AAAA is negative or the bounded resolution phase expires.
Prefer IPv6 for transport to a configured DNS server before trying that server over IPv4.
requirements.reason: This library requests A and AAAA data through the host resolver and never owns DNS-server addresses or selects the IP family used to transport DNS queries.

requirements.summary: Do not impose an explicit software limit on the number of configured DNS servers.
requirements.reason: DNS server configuration and its capacity belong to the operating system resolver; this library neither stores nor truncates a DNS-server list.

requirements.summary: If hardware requires a DNS-server limit, retain at least one server address from each IP family.
requirements.reason: The operating system resolver owns any hardware-specific DNS-server limit, and no DNS-server address list crosses this library boundary.

requirements.summary: Sort resolved destinations with RFC 6724 Destination Address Selection before family interleaving.
When route round-trip-time history exists, prefer destinations whose route has a lower expected RTT.
requirements.reason: The finite per-connection scheduler keeps no persistent route RTT history, so the condition that activates this additional sorting rule never occurs.

requirements.summary: When destination-use history exists, prefer addresses that were successfully used before unused addresses.
requirements.reason: The scheduler deliberately retains no destination-use history between connections, so there is no historical address state from which to derive this preference.

requirements.summary: Do not apply destination RTT or prior-use history across different network interfaces.
requirements.reason: No destination RTT or prior-use history is persisted at all, and consequently no historical record can be shared across network interfaces.

requirements.summary: Flush historical destination-selection data whenever the device changes its attached network.
requirements.reason: The scheduler is created for one connection race and persists no historical destination-selection data that could survive a network change.

requirements.summary: Interleave IPv4 and IPv6 destinations after sorting, while preserving the preferred family at the head.
Start connection attempts one at a time with a finite delay rather than launching all candidates simultaneously.
After authenticating and adopting one candidate, cancel and join every losing resolver and connection worker.
After a candidate wins, do not start connection work for destinations that have not yet been attempted.
Continue processing late DNS replies briefly after a connection succeeds so a resolver cache can be populated.
requirements.reason: The library owns no DNS cache and uses private supervised resolver workers, so it cancels and joins those workers immediately after a winner to preserve the finite lifetime contract. The host resolver remains free to maintain its own cache.

requirements.summary: Apply a lower bound to accelerated connection-attempt spacing even after an earlier candidate fails.
Never start a subsequent connection attempt within ten milliseconds of the preceding attempt.
Keep connection-attempt delay below a finite upper bound and within the original total connection deadline.
Do not cancel an already-started connection merely because a later DNS update removes its destination.
requirements.reason: Each address family supplies one immutable bounded result to a connection race; the API accepts no later DNS removal or TTL update that could trigger this condition.

requirements.summary: Remove an unstarted destination when a later DNS update removes that address from the answer set.
requirements.reason: Each address family supplies one immutable bounded result to a connection race; the API accepts no later DNS removal or TTL update from which to remove queued work.

requirements.summary: On a platform without 464XLAT, apply the section recommendations for IPv6-only NAT64 and DNS64 networks.
requirements.reason: This user-space transport delegates name resolution and NAT64 synthesis to the operating system and does not inspect interfaces or synthesize IPv4-embedded IPv6 destinations.

requirements.summary: Enable special NAT64 network behavior only after detecting a network where that behavior is needed.
requirements.reason: The library exposes no special NAT64 synthesis or reachability mode, so there is no such feature that could be enabled on an undetected network.

requirements.summary: Keep the configured minimum connection-attempt delay at or above ten milliseconds.
Increase Happy Eyeballs delay values over client releases as IPv6 deployment quality improves.
requirements.reason: Version 0.1.0 uses deterministic observed values of 50 milliseconds for resolution, 100 milliseconds for failure acceleration, and 250 milliseconds for normal attempt spacing. It does not infer release age or global IPv6 quality, and keeps these bounded values stable for reproducible resource behavior.

requirements.summary: A client should close an idle connection whose Origin Set is a proper subset.

entries.reason: The correction removes duplicate all-zero state rows from three optional cross-check tables. Section 4.1.1 remains the authoritative table-construction algorithm, so the wire grammar and decoder behavior do not change.

requirements.summary: A receiver accepts every value of the seven unused Version Negotiation first-byte bits and assigns them no semantics.
A Version Negotiation packet with no Supported Version field or a truncated final field is rejected before it can change endpoint state.
The listener copies the received Source Connection ID into the Version Negotiation Destination Connection ID.
The listener copies the received Destination Connection ID into the Version Negotiation Source Connection ID.
A client can tentatively change only to an originally offered compatible version and accepts that choice only after authenticated transport parameters prove the server's version set.

entries.reason: The verified correction makes the preferred-address sequence-number offset explicit. This server cannot advertise a preferred_address at runtime, so its local issuer starts NEW_CONNECTION_ID at one and the correction changes no reachable current-source behavior; the related normative clauses remain Open.

The verified correction distinguishes an authenticated, readable Retry token that fails address validation from an unreadable token. Current routing now sends protected INVALID_TOKEN only for an authenticated Retry token that fails validation, while missing or unauthenticatable tokens retain the Retry path.

The verified correction adds the congestion-control marker to CONNECTION_CLOSE in the RFC 9000 summary table. Current source already excludes CONNECTION_CLOSE from ack-eliciting and in-flight treatment under RFC 9002, so accepting the table correction requires no behavior change.

The verified editorial correction removes the 0-RTT marker from RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID. Current source already rejects an authenticated RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID in 0-RTT, so the corrected table creates no behavior change.
The held report proposes broader advice for the Version Negotiation Fixed Bit. It is recorded as reviewed but is not a verified correction, so this inventory applies no new current-source behavior.

The held report proposes an explicit denial-of-service cross-reference for excessive PATH_CHALLENGE input. It is recorded for future document update review and does not replace the published normative text in this inventory.

The held report clarifies that Section 19.7 governs NEW_TOKEN even when Section 12.5 discusses 0-RTT. The report requests no intended behavior change, and this inventory continues to enumerate both published clauses independently.

The held editorial report would remove a contradictory ECN exception. It has not been verified, so the published uppercase obligation remains authoritative and no new behavior is attributed to the report.
The RFC Editor rejected the proposed max_ack_delay rewrite. The published acknowledgement obligation remains authoritative and the rejected text creates no implementation behavior.

standards.title: QUIC Loss Detection and Congestion Control

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.

requirements.summary: An ACK that does not newly acknowledge its largest packet does not update the RTT estimator.
An ACK creates no RTT sample unless it newly acknowledges at least one ack-eliciting packet.
The first real RTT sample initializes min_rtt to exactly the latest observed RTT.
Every later sample retains the lesser of the existing min_rtt and latest_rtt.
Persistent congestion refreshes min_rtt from the newest authenticated RTT sample.
The implementation refreshes min_rtt only on the explicit persistent-congestion transition.
Before handshake confirmation, RTT adjustment does not cap ACK delay at max_ack_delay.
The normative adjustment procedure ignores the peer maximum ACK delay until confirmation.
After confirmation, RTT adjustment uses the lesser of reported and maximum ACK delay.
ACK delay is never subtracted when doing so would make the adjusted sample smaller than min_rtt.
Locally postponed pre-confirmation ACK processing should subtract its local key-wait delay.
requirements.reason: This stack never queues an encrypted ACK for processing before its packet-protection keys exist; only successfully decrypted packets reach recovery, so no local key-wait interval exists to subtract.

requirements.summary: Packet-threshold loss detection starts at the recommended distance of three packets.
The fixed packet reordering threshold cannot be configured below three packets.
An earlier in-flight packet is declared lost after a later same-space packet is acknowledged and the time threshold passes.
The time loss threshold is always at least the local timer granularity.
A not-yet-lost packet before the largest ACK schedules its remaining time-threshold deadline.
Time-threshold loss detection uses the recommended nine-eighths RTT multiplier.
The live recovery owner uses the recommended one millisecond timer granularity.
PTO expiry increments backoff and requests probes without declaring any outstanding packet lost.
The four-times RTT variation component floors every PTO base at timer granularity.
The connection deadline selects the earlier Initial or Handshake recovery timer.

entries.reason: The correction changes only the final quality value in an Accept precedence example. This library transports Accept fields but does not implement the example content-negotiation selection algorithm.

The corrected ranges-specifier ABNF permits optional whitespace after the equals sign. The public library does not parse or synthesize byte-range syntax, so the correction changes no implemented behavior.
The correction replaces an accidental Accept-Encoding reference with Accept-Charset in explanatory prose. Header fields remain opaque at this boundary, so no parser or serializer branch changes.
The correction documents the already normative deprecation of CN-ID in the changes appendix. It introduces no behavior beyond the certificate-identity requirements already inventoried from the body.

The accepted text makes 308 method preservation explicit. Redirect regeneration shares the method-preserving 307 and 308 branch; the tests cover method preservation and select the 308 non-replayable-body path.
The correction removes a change-log statement that belongs to RFC 9112. The absolute-form rule itself remains in RFC 9112 and is separately inventoried there.

The report proposes spelling the field-line combination separator as comma plus space. The implementation preserves received field lines and does not expose a generic combined-field-value operation, so no behavior claim is made.
The report documents normalization choices in the collected ABNF without changing the language recognized by the grammar. It has no wire-behavior impact.
The RFC Editor rejected the report because RFC 9112 Section 7.1.2 exists; the published cross-reference remains authoritative.
The proposed addition of 205 to the generic content-presence list was rejected as contrary to the working group decision; the published semantics remain authoritative.
The proposed rewrite of Content-Length forwarding rules was rejected. The published sender and recipient obligations remain unchanged and are inventoried from the RFC text.
The proposed recursive-redirect processing rule was rejected and therefore adds no protocol requirement.
The proposal to extend valid HTTP status codes through 999 was rejected; the published 100 through 599 range remains authoritative.
The wording change from applied to processed was rejected and has no protocol behavior impact.

standards.review_scope: The canonical RFC text has a complete, contiguous inventory of 254 uppercase mandatory and advisory BCP 14 occurrences outside the keyword convention. Every occurrence has an exact line, column, ordinal, and full SHA-256 clause fingerprint. Existing current-source evidence is preserved where independently established; all other clauses remain Open, so map_complete remains false until role-specific executable evidence closes them.

normative_inventory.scope: Atomic uppercase BCP 14 mandatory and advisory clauses; MAY and OPTIONAL are excluded.
normative_inventory.role_model: Client and server HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 endpoints. A single role is assigned only when the grammatical subject is unambiguous; endpoint, sender, receiver, peer, intermediary, and implementation duties conservatively retain both endpoint roles when the text does not fix a direction.

requirements.summary: An endpoint that chooses to terminate an HTTP/3 connection first sends GOAWAY so accepted work is unambiguous.
requirements.reason: Every planned public HTTP/3 termination now selects a role-correct two-stage GOAWAY path. Client close and immediate server stop explicitly settle application work; graceful server stop preserves accepted work. All three wait for payload-free application-space acknowledgement under one immutable monotonic drain deadline before exact H3_NO_ERROR. Deadline, protocol, transport, and owner-loss paths remain abortive. Injected-clock state tests and synchronized raw UDP peer tests assert GOAWAY order and the following peer-observed close code without sleeps or retry polling; current-source execution remains a qualification gate rather than a claim in this source review.

entries.reason: The verified correction replaces the nonexistent path-absolute production with HTTP absolute-path, which permits a path beginning with two slashes. The validator accepts every nonempty HTTP path other than the method-specific asterisk exception. The retained positive path test reaches that policy boundary; an exact double-slash regression case remains necessary before the related normative map can be closed.

The verified correction removes the nonexistent HTTP/2 PADDING-frame reference while retaining Padding fields and HTTP/3 padding choices. It changes explanatory security text without changing an HTTP/3 wire requirement.

The verified correction applies misplaced-GOAWAY rejection to either endpoint instead of only clients. Request-stream dispatch rejects control-only known frames for both roles, and the retained role-error test exercises that shared rejection boundary; a GOAWAY-specific wrong-stream case remains necessary before the exact clause can be marked implemented.

The report proposes an exception for reserved HTTP/2 setting identifiers. Its status is Reported, so it is recorded for review but does not replace the published text or establish a new current-source behavior claim.

The RFC Editor rejected the proposed below-to-above change because an intermediary can still reject a message below one hop limit when the next hop advertises a smaller limit. The published text remains authoritative.
The RFC Editor rejected the proposed server-side stream-ID check because client-to-server GOAWAY carries a push ID in its own namespace. The rejected text creates no implementation obligation.

standards.review_scope: The pinned inventory contains 54 atomic mandatory and advisory occurrences. Current-source review classifies 20 as Implemented, 30 as NotApplicable, 4 as Open, and none as DocumentedDeviation. requirements.summary: P-256, P-384, and P-521 public inputs must receive partial public-key validation.

requirements.reason: The closed OHTTP profile has no PSK or DeriveKeyPair input; its HPKE info and exporter context are fixed strings plus a seven-byte header and remain below 64 bytes. Fixed vectors exercise both labeled contexts.

requirements.summary: Applications claiming resistance to key-compromise impersonation should add an explicit protection.
requirements.reason: The OHTTP base-mode profile does not authenticate a sender and makes no key-compromise impersonation resistance claim. Applications cannot request an authenticated HPKE mode through this API.

requirements.summary: A KEM used by HPKE must provide the security properties required by the HPKE construction.
requirements.reason: The profile admits only the registered DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), implements its labeled extract-and-expand construction, and validates low-order inputs. Fixed vectors and hostile public keys distinguish the required KEM behavior.

requirements.summary: The KEM shared secret must be a uniformly random Nsecret-byte string.

The verified correction clamps the serialized X25519 private-key values printed in Appendix A. X25519 already clamps internally and the corrected values produce identical public keys, so this fixes vector presentation without changing derived wire values.

The verified correction narrows the stated security notions for authenticated HPKE and records that Insider-Auth is not achieved. This library exposes only the OHTTP base-mode profile, so the correction changes no supported authentication-mode behavior.

The verified correction distinguishes the HPKE info parameter from the internal KDF info string and replaces field terminology with parameter. The existing labeled schedule already supplies each value at its specified position, so the clarification changes no bytes.

The verified correction makes the KEM-derived suite identifier explicit inside X25519 and X448 DeriveKeyPair. The OHTTP surface generates ephemeral keys directly and does not expose DeriveKeyPair, so no supported behavior or vector changes.
The verified editorial correction changes a pseudocode reference from below to above because IncrementSeq is already printed earlier. It creates no protocol or API behavior.

This held report proposes raising a recommended static-allocation input limit from 64 to 66 bytes to fit appendix vectors. Held status does not replace the published recommendation, and the OHTTP API does not impose either limit.

requirements.summary: The encoder emits field representations in the input field-section order.
The encoder does not insert or duplicate when that growth would evict an unacknowledged referenced entry.
The encoder never risks more streams than the peer SETTINGS_QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS value.
A decoder rejects blocked-stream use above its advertised bound as QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
QPACK instructions are submitted as one bounded resource write and retained when full credit is unavailable.
The decoder returns field lines in representation order.
Blocked field-section data should remain charged to receive flow control until decoder state arrives.
requirements.reason: The public QUIC stream adapter delivers already-accounted bounded chunks before QPACK can inspect Required Insert Count. HTTP/3 therefore retains those bytes in a per-stream and aggregate connection budget instead of pretending credit was not consumed; exceeding either ceiling fails closed.

requirements.summary: A Required Insert Count smaller than the referenced dynamic state causes QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
Completing a field section with dynamic references queues a Section Acknowledgment.
Evicted or out-of-range dynamic references in field sections cause QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
Evicted or missing dynamic references on the encoder stream cause QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR.
An invalid static-table index in a field representation causes QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
An invalid static-table index on the encoder stream causes QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR.
Duplicate name-value entries remain valid dynamic-table insertions.
Capacity changes and insertions cannot evict a referenced dynamic entry.
An encoder-stream insertion larger than active capacity is rejected as QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR.
The encoder cannot set dynamic capacity above the decoder-advertised maximum.
A server accepting HTTP/3 0-RTT with remembered non-zero capacity repeats that setting.
requirements.reason: The current API can resume QUIC with 0-RTT keys but never exposes or sends HTTP/3 field sections before authenticated peer SETTINGS are received. Therefore no QPACK encoder state or remembered QPACK setting is used in early data.

requirements.summary: A zero maximum dynamic-table capacity prevents every insertion.
A zero maximum capacity produces no encoder-stream instructions.
The prefixed-integer codec accepts the complete unsigned 62-bit QUIC integer range.
Each endpoint creates at most one QPACK encoder stream and one QPACK decoder stream.
A second peer encoder or decoder stream causes H3_STREAM_CREATION_ERROR.
The endpoint never sends FIN on its QPACK encoder or decoder critical stream.
The endpoint does not issue STOP_SENDING for a peer QPACK critical stream.
FIN or reset on a QPACK critical stream causes H3_CLOSED_CRITICAL_STREAM.
Both QPACK critical stream types are accepted even when configured table capacity is zero.
A Set Dynamic Table Capacity value cannot exceed the peer's configured ceiling.
The decoder maps an excessive capacity instruction to QPACK_ENCODER_STREAM_ERROR.
Reducing capacity cannot evict any entry still held by an unacknowledged field section.
Acknowledging a stream with no outstanding dynamic section causes QPACK_DECODER_STREAM_ERROR.
A zero or excessive Insert Count Increment causes QPACK_DECODER_STREAM_ERROR.
An Encoded Insert Count impossible for a conformant encoder causes QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
The encoder never emits a field-section prefix whose reconstructed Base is negative.
A sign bit with Required Insert Count not above Delta Base is rejected as QPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED.
A field marked never-indexed is encoded only with a literal representation.
A QPACK intermediary forwarding a received N-bit field retains a literal never-indexed representation.
requirements.reason: The library does not expose an automatic HTTP intermediary that forwards decoded QPACK fields. Client proxy configuration selects an outbound transport but never re-encodes peer response fields as a new request.

requirements.summary: An intermediary never converts a received never-indexed literal into an indexed representation.
requirements.reason: No automatic intermediary forwarding API consumes decoded QPACK never-index metadata, so the conditional re-encoding operation is unavailable rather than silently dropping the protection.

requirements.summary: QPACK re-encoding by an intermediary uses a literal with the N bit set.
requirements.reason: The product does not provide automatic intermediary re-encoding; callers can explicitly preserve the typed never-index bit, but no decoded peer field is implicitly forwarded.

requirements.summary: Translation to HPACK preserves received QPACK N-bit fields as HPACK never-indexed literals.
requirements.reason: The library intentionally has no automatic HTTP/3-to-HTTP/2 intermediary translation path, so it cannot consume and accidentally weaken received QPACK never-index metadata.

requirements.summary: Integer and string limits cover the configured maximum field-section size while remaining finite.
Values above configured decode limits map to decompression or the matching critical-stream QPACK error code.

entries.reason: The verified correction makes Required Insert Count one greater than the largest zero-based dynamic index, matching the normative algorithm.
The proposal changes CORS spellings and removes an entry, but it is held rather than verified and cannot alter the published fixed QPACK wire indices without an updating standard.

standards.title: The Proxy-Status HTTP Response Header Field

requirements.summary: Every accepted Proxy-Status list member identifies its intermediary with a Structured Fields String or Token.
The safe append operation retains the existing origin-to-client intermediary chain before adding the local member.
The role-aware field generator refuses Proxy-Status generation by an origin server.
The role-aware generator rejects trailer placement when the Proxy-Status value could still be sent in headers.
Every generated trailer member must match a character-identical intermediary member announced in the header section.
Unknown parameters do not affect registered semantics and the default public diagnostic view removes them.
A generating intermediary selects the most specific registered proxy error that accurately describes its failure.
requirements.reason: The codec has no transport or application failure context from which to infer a proxy error type; it preserves the caller-selected token exactly so policy can select a deployment-accurate registered or extension value.

requirements.summary: An intermediary-generated HTTP response normally uses the response status recommended for its selected proxy error type.
requirements.reason: This module encodes and decodes a field value but never chooses or generates an HTTP response status; that response-policy decision remains outside the value codec.

requirements.summary: The next-protocol parameter accepts only a nonempty bounded ALPN identifier represented as Token or Byte Sequence.
An ALPN identifier representable as an ASCII Structured Fields Token is rejected in Byte Sequence form.
The received-status registered parameter accepts only an integer HTTP status value.

requirements.summary: The policy-aware generator rejects Cache-Status on a locally generated response unless that response is based on stored state.

Every accepted Cache-Status list member identifies its cache with a Structured Fields String or Token.
A generating cache selects the most specific forward reason that its cache-decision state can determine.

requirements.summary: SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES accepts only the wire values zero and one.
An invalid SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES value is classified as an HTTP/2 protocol connection error.
An endpoint using SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES sends it only in its first SETTINGS frame.
A sender cannot change SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES after its first SETTINGS frame.
A server receiving SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES equal to one ignores RFC 7540 priority signals.
Before peer SETTINGS arrive, a client sends both legacy and extensible priority signals.
requirements.reason: The client never generates legacy RFC 7540 priority frames; it preserves an application-supplied Priority field and avoids allocating or emitting the obsolete dependency tree solely during SETTINGS discovery.

requirements.summary: A client stops legacy HTTP/2 priority signals after the server opts out of RFC 7540 priorities.
A client does not send HTTP/2 PRIORITY_UPDATE when the peer retains legacy priority signaling.
A server applies default urgency and incremental values when a request omits those priority parameters.
Unknown priority parameters and known parameters with out-of-range or unexpected value types are ignored.
A client fetching a multi-resource document assigns default urgency to its main resource.
requirements.reason: The protocol library cannot infer which application request is the main resource of a document; it preserves explicit Priority fields and otherwise uses the protocol default without inventing document semantics.

requirements.summary: Urgency seven is not assigned to a response that affects user interaction.
requirements.reason: The library cannot determine whether a request affects user interaction, so it validates urgency as the complete zero-through-seven wire range and leaves semantic assignment to the application.

requirements.summary: A server retains only the latest bounded PRIORITY_UPDATE for a stream that has not opened yet.
The HTTP/2 PRIORITY_UPDATE frame header carries stream identifier zero.
A nonzero HTTP/2 PRIORITY_UPDATE frame stream identifier is a protocol connection error.
An HTTP/2 client targets only live or idle request streams with PRIORITY_UPDATE.
requirements.reason: The HTTP/2 client has no outbound PRIORITY_UPDATE operation; application priority is carried in the request Priority field, so it cannot select a request-stream target for this frame.

requirements.summary: Active streams plus retained idle PRIORITY_UPDATE targets do not exceed the peer stream concurrency limit.
An HTTP/2 PRIORITY_UPDATE that exceeds the bounded active-plus-idle target limit causes a protocol connection error.
An HTTP/2 client targets only reserved or half-closed push streams with PRIORITY_UPDATE.

requirements.summary: An endpoint sends no DATAGRAM frame until a nonzero peer max_datagram_frame_size has been authenticated, including remembered state for 0-RTT.
A sender bounds the entire encoded DATAGRAM frame by the peer's advertised value and the current path budget.
Receiving DATAGRAM without locally advertised support is classified as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
Receiving a DATAGRAM frame larger than the local advertised limit is classified as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
The default receive policy advertises 65535 so every DATAGRAM fitting a QUIC packet is admissible before tighter endpoint limits.
A server accepts early data only when the current remembered 0-RTT parameter set is compatible; the equality-only policy is stricter than the required nondecrease.
A resumed client compares the fresh max_datagram_frame_size, treating omission as zero, with its ticket-authenticated value before overwriting it.
A fresh server DATAGRAM limit below the stored 0-RTT value, including omission, produces PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
HTTP/3 makes QUIC DATAGRAM absence an explicit typed negotiation failure while allowing explicitly negotiated Capsule-only delivery.
A queued DATAGRAM enters the bounded application frame queue immediately and is emitted at the first congestion-, pacing-, recovery-, ACK-, and path-budget opportunity.
A valid DATAGRAM becomes an ordered application event in the same receive transition when finite memory admission succeeds; overload is explicitly droppable and counted.
DATAGRAM application data is legal only at 0-RTT or 1-RTT packet-protection levels.
Applications should be able to prioritize DATAGRAM frames relative to one another and streams.
requirements.reason: The stable 0.1.0 API intentionally exposes one bounded FIFO DATAGRAM lane and fair stream scheduling, but no relative DATAGRAM priority contract yet. Adding priorities before expiry, starvation, and scheduler traces are specified would create an unauditable ordering promise; the current deterministic queue is covered while the extension remains explicit residual work.

requirements.summary: A DATAGRAM-only application packet is ack-eliciting but uses the bounded delayed-ACK policy until packet count, reordering, ECN, or max_ack_delay requires an ACK.
DATAGRAM frames enter the common congestion and pacing budget and are delayed in their finite queue or dropped when a changed path can no longer carry them.
The security restatement that every DATAGRAM payload is protected by 0-RTT or 1-RTT keys is enforced at the authenticated packet boundary.

requirements.summary: A non-empty grease_quic_bit value causes a TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR connection error.
Both advertising endpoint roles accept authenticated packets whose QUIC Bit is zero.
After negotiation, each role derives an unpredictable QUIC Bit from protected secret material and packet number.
The client never clears the QUIC Bit before processing current peer support.
A server can clear the QUIC Bit only after processing the current client's transport parameter.
Peer support starts false in every new server connection and is never inherited from an earlier connection.
Packet protection keeps the QUIC Bit set until the sending connection knows peer support.
Any extension assigning semantics to the QUIC Bit must negotiate before acting on it.
requirements.reason: This implementation assigns no alternate semantic to the QUIC Bit; it implements only RFC 9287 greasing and treats the bit as no application signal.

requirements.summary: Recipients reject field names or values that violate the HTTP/2 generic field validity rules.
Extension pseudo-fields precede every regular field line when the optional extension form is supported.
requirements.reason: The bounded codec does not opt into the optional extension pseudo-field form: every colon-bearing field name is rejected, so no accepted message can contain a pseudo-field to order.

requirements.summary: Construction normally removes connection-related fields that have no connection effect in a binary message.
requirements.reason: The general-purpose codec preserves syntactically valid connection fields so callers can capture an exchanged protocol message, an exception RFC 9292 explicitly permits; higher-level protocol adapters remain responsible for hop-by-hop normalization.
